quests.hint: 'Nevertheless' at the start signals a contrast with something said just before.
quests.explanation: 'Nevertheless' is a more formal alternative to 'however' or 'but', often used to introduce a contrasting point despite what was previously acknowledged. It's common in essays, articles, and formal speech.
quests.textToSpeak: Nevertheless, many companies continue to prioritise short-term profits over the long-term wellbeing of their staff.
quests.correctAnswer: Nevertheless, many companies continue to prioritise short-term profits over the long-term wellbeing of their staff.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Nevertheless' at the start signals a contrast with something said just before.

quests.hint: 'Whereas' sets up a direct contrast between two groups — stress it clearly.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' introduces a formal contrast between two different situations or groups, often used in comparisons. It's more precise and structured than simply using 'but'.
quests.textToSpeak: Whereas older generations valued job security above almost everything else, many younger workers now prioritise flexibility.
quests.correctAnswer: Whereas older generations valued job security above almost everything else, many younger workers now prioritise flexibility.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Whereas' sets up a direct contrast between two groups — stress it clearly.

quests.hint: 'Given that' introduces a widely accepted fact as the basis for a conclusion.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces a reason or fact that the rest of the sentence builds on, similar to 'because' but slightly more formal. It's especially common when presenting an argument.
quests.textToSpeak: Given that most people check their phones within minutes of waking, sustained focus has become genuinely harder to maintain.
quests.correctAnswer: Given that most people check their phones within minutes of waking, sustained focus has become genuinely harder to maintain.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Given that' introduces a widely accepted fact as the basis for a conclusion.

quests.hint: 'Whether or not' shows the outcome is true regardless of the two possibilities.
quests.explanation: 'Whether or not' expresses that something is true no matter which of two possibilities is the case. This phrase adds a note of critical, slightly pointed observation.
quests.textToSpeak: Social media platforms are designed to capture attention, whether or not that serves the user's actual wellbeing.
quests.correctAnswer: Social media platforms are designed to capture attention, whether or not that serves the user's actual wellbeing.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Whether or not' shows the outcome is true regardless of the two possibilities.

quests.hint: 'It's worth remembering that' introduces a helpful, grounding reminder.
quests.explanation: 'It's worth remembering that' is a useful structure for reintroducing an important but easily forgotten fact. 'Algorithm' is now everyday vocabulary for the rules that decide what content you see online.
quests.textToSpeak: It's worth remembering that an algorithm has no real interest in whether you feel better after scrolling.
quests.correctAnswer: It's worth remembering that an algorithm has no real interest in whether you feel better after scrolling.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'It's worth remembering that' introduces a helpful, grounding reminder.

quests.hint: 'However brief' means 'no matter how short' — a compact, advanced structure.
quests.explanation: 'However' plus an adjective, without a full clause, is a compact way of saying 'no matter how [adjective] it is'. 'Chip away at' is a vivid phrasal verb for something being slowly worn down.
quests.textToSpeak: Notifications are deliberately engineered to interrupt, and interruption, however brief, quietly chips away at real concentration.
quests.correctAnswer: Notifications are deliberately engineered to interrupt, and interruption, however brief, quietly chips away at real concentration.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'However brief' means 'no matter how short' — a compact, advanced structure.

quests.hint: 'That said' softly introduces a balancing point after a previous idea.
quests.explanation: 'That said' is a conversational way to introduce a contrasting or balancing thought, softer than 'however'. 'The extent to which' is a formal structure for describing how much something is true.
quests.textToSpeak: That said, blaming technology alone overlooks the extent to which people choose how they use it.
quests.correctAnswer: That said, blaming technology alone overlooks the extent to which people choose how they use it.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'That said' softly introduces a balancing point after a previous idea.

quests.hint: 'In spite of' works exactly like 'despite', followed by a noun phrase.
quests.explanation: 'In spite of' and 'despite' are interchangeable, both followed by a noun or -ing form rather than a full clause. This sentence makes an ironic point about modern productivity culture.
quests.textToSpeak: In spite of countless productivity apps, many people report feeling busier and more distracted than ever.
quests.correctAnswer: In spite of countless productivity apps, many people report feeling busier and more distracted than ever.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'In spite of' works exactly like 'despite', followed by a noun phrase.

quests.hint: 'It turns out' is inserted mid-sentence, almost like an aside — pause briefly around it.
quests.explanation: 'It turns out' can be inserted into the middle of a sentence as a kind of aside, adding a note of discovered surprise. This is a natural feature of thoughtful, reflective spoken English.
quests.textToSpeak: Simplicity, it turns out, is often harder to design than complexity, despite how it looks from the outside.
quests.correctAnswer: Simplicity, it turns out, is often harder to design than complexity, despite how it looks from the outside.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'It turns out' is inserted mid-sentence, almost like an aside — pause briefly around it.

quests.hint: 'Tolerates' here means 'allows to continue', often with a hint of disapproval.
quests.explanation: 'Tolerate' means to allow something to happen or continue, often something not ideal, carrying a slightly critical tone. 'Collaboration' refers to people working together effectively towards a shared goal.
quests.textToSpeak: A workplace that tolerates gossip and blame will rarely build the trust needed for honest collaboration.
quests.correctAnswer: A workplace that tolerates gossip and blame will rarely build the trust needed for honest collaboration.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Tolerates' here means 'allows to continue', often with a hint of disapproval.

quests.hint: 'Those who never do' avoids repeating 'admit their own mistakes' a second time.
quests.explanation: 'Those who...' is a useful way to refer back to a group without repeating a full description. 'Genuine' emphasises that the respect is real and sincere, not just superficial politeness.
quests.textToSpeak: Leaders who admit their own mistakes tend to earn more genuine respect than those who never do.
quests.correctAnswer: Leaders who admit their own mistakes tend to earn more genuine respect than those who never do.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Those who never do' avoids repeating 'admit their own mistakes' a second time.

quests.hint: 'However old-fashioned it sounds' concedes a point while still standing firm.
quests.explanation: 'However' plus an adjective and clause concedes a possible objection while still maintaining the main point. This is a persuasive technique: acknowledging doubt without abandoning your position.
quests.textToSpeak: Praise given in public and criticism given in private remains surprisingly good advice, however old-fashioned it sounds.
quests.correctAnswer: Praise given in public and criticism given in private remains surprisingly good advice, however old-fashioned it sounds.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'However old-fashioned it sounds' concedes a point while still standing firm.

quests.hint: 'Resting on' is a metaphor meaning 'based on' or 'supported by'.
quests.explanation: 'Rest on something' figuratively means to be based on or supported by it, much like a building rests on its foundation. This metaphor makes an abstract idea about evidence feel more concrete.
quests.textToSpeak: However convincing an argument sounds at first, it's always worth asking what evidence it's actually resting on.
quests.correctAnswer: However convincing an argument sounds at first, it's always worth asking what evidence it's actually resting on.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Resting on' is a metaphor meaning 'based on' or 'supported by'.

quests.hint: The contrast between 'story' and 'spreadsheet' makes the point memorable.
quests.explanation: This sentence contrasts two very different, vivid images, a story and a spreadsheet, to make a point about human psychology feel concrete and memorable. Persuasive writing often relies on this kind of contrast.
quests.textToSpeak: People are generally far more persuaded by a good story than by a spreadsheet full of statistics.
quests.correctAnswer: People are generally far more persuaded by a good story than by a spreadsheet full of statistics.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] The contrast between 'story' and 'spreadsheet' makes the point memorable.

quests.hint: 'At least until' shows a limit to how long something remains true.
quests.explanation: 'At least until' introduces a limit or condition on a previous statement, showing that a situation may change. 'A sharp question' is one that gets straight to the weak point of an argument.
quests.textToSpeak: A confident tone can make a weak argument sound convincing, at least until someone asks a sharp question.
quests.correctAnswer: A confident tone can make a weak argument sound convincing, at least until someone asks a sharp question.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'At least until' shows a limit to how long something remains true.

quests.hint: 'Misunderstood by' is passive, keeping the focus on the cultures, not the people judging them.
quests.explanation: This passive structure, 'misunderstood by', keeps the emphasis on the cultures being judged, rather than on the people doing the judging. This subtle choice reflects the sentence's sympathetic tone.
quests.textToSpeak: Cultures that value silence in conversation are often misunderstood by those who consider it awkward or rude.
quests.correctAnswer: Cultures that value silence in conversation are often misunderstood by those who consider it awkward or rude.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Misunderstood by' is passive, keeping the focus on the cultures, not the people judging them.

quests.hint: 'What counts as polite' works as the subject of the whole sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Count as' means to be considered or classified as something, useful for discussing how definitions shift between cultures. 'Oddly distant' and 'even cold' build in intensity, moving from mild to stronger criticism.
quests.textToSpeak: What counts as polite in one country can seem oddly distant or even cold in another.
quests.correctAnswer: What counts as polite in one country can seem oddly distant or even cold in another.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'What counts as polite' works as the subject of the whole sentence.

quests.hint: 'Every bit as much as' is a stronger, more emphatic version of 'just as much as'.
quests.explanation: 'Every bit as much as' intensifies a comparison of equality, stronger than the plainer 'just as much as'. 'Unspoken rules' refers to social norms that are understood but never explicitly stated.
quests.textToSpeak: Learning a culture's unspoken rules often matters every bit as much as learning its language.
quests.correctAnswer: Learning a culture's unspoken rules often matters every bit as much as learning its language.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Every bit as much as' is a stronger, more emphatic version of 'just as much as'.

quests.hint: 'Not X so much as Y' shows Y is the truer, more accurate explanation.
quests.explanation: 'Not X so much as Y' is a nuanced way to correct a common assumption, suggesting the real cause is slightly different from what people usually think. This structure adds psychological depth to a familiar idea.
quests.textToSpeak: Most people don't actually fear failure itself so much as they fear being seen to fail.
quests.correctAnswer: Most people don't actually fear failure itself so much as they fear being seen to fail.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Not X so much as Y' shows Y is the truer, more accurate explanation.

quests.hint: The semicolon connects two closely related ideas — pause briefly, don't stop fully.
quests.explanation: This sentence gently corrects a common misconception using 'rarely... more often', a persuasive pairing. 'A quiet way of avoiding discomfort' offers a more compassionate explanation than simply calling someone lazy.
quests.textToSpeak: Procrastination is rarely simply about laziness; more often, it's a quiet way of avoiding discomfort.
quests.correctAnswer: Procrastination is rarely simply about laziness; more often, it's a quiet way of avoiding discomfort.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] The semicolon connects two closely related ideas — pause briefly, don't stop fully.

quests.hint: 'Setting a smaller, more specific goal' as a subject pairs with 'tends to be'.
quests.explanation: 'Vague' means unclear or not specific, the opposite of 'specific' used earlier in the sentence. This deliberate contrast reinforces the sentence's practical advice about goal-setting.
quests.textToSpeak: Setting a smaller, more specific goal tends to be far more motivating than setting a vague one.
quests.correctAnswer: Setting a smaller, more specific goal tends to be far more motivating than setting a vague one.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Setting a smaller, more specific goal' as a subject pairs with 'tends to be'.

quests.hint: This is a long, information-dense sentence — keep a calm, even pace throughout.
quests.explanation: 'In-demand' describes something currently wanted or valued, especially skills in a job market. 'Given the pace at which' introduces a reason based on how quickly something is happening.
quests.textToSpeak: Given the pace at which technology changes, some of today's most in-demand skills may be irrelevant within a decade.
quests.correctAnswer: Given the pace at which technology changes, some of today's most in-demand skills may be irrelevant within a decade.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] This is a long, information-dense sentence — keep a calm, even pace throughout.

quests.hint: 'Sheer' adds emphasis, meaning 'pure' or 'complete', before 'ability'.
quests.explanation: 'Sheer' is an intensifier used before a noun to emphasise its scale or completeness. 'Fixed skill' contrasts with the adaptable, ongoing 'ability to learn', reinforcing the sentence's main point.
quests.textToSpeak: Employers increasingly seem to value the sheer ability to learn quickly over almost any single fixed skill.
quests.correctAnswer: Employers increasingly seem to value the sheer ability to learn quickly over almost any single fixed skill.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Sheer' adds emphasis, meaning 'pure' or 'complete', before 'ability'.

quests.hint: 'More than raw talent' interrupts the sentence to add a quick comparison.
quests.explanation: Inserting a short comparative phrase like 'more than raw talent' directly after the subject adds emphasis without needing a separate sentence. 'Over the long run' means across an extended period of time.
quests.textToSpeak: Curiosity, more than raw talent, tends to determine who keeps improving over the long run.
quests.correctAnswer: Curiosity, more than raw talent, tends to determine who keeps improving over the long run.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'More than raw talent' interrupts the sentence to add a quick comparison.

quests.hint: 'Say more than' is used figuratively — a pause doesn't literally speak.
quests.explanation: This sentence figuratively describes a silent pause as being able to 'say' something, a poetic use of language for emphasis. 'Well-placed' describes something positioned at just the right moment.
quests.textToSpeak: A well-placed pause in a conversation can say more than the sentence that follows it.
quests.correctAnswer: A well-placed pause in a conversation can say more than the sentence that follows it.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Say more than' is used figuratively — a pause doesn't literally speak.

quests.hint: 'Rather than' contrasts two possible responses to a conversation.
quests.explanation: 'Rather than' introduces an alternative that wasn't chosen, contrasting two possible behaviours. This sentence offers a specific, practical tip rather than just a general statement about listening.
quests.textToSpeak: The best listeners tend to ask one more question rather than immediately offering their opinion.
quests.correctAnswer: The best listeners tend to ask one more question rather than immediately offering their opinion.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Rather than' contrasts two possible responses to a conversation.

quests.hint: The contrast between 'rarely' and 'precisely' highlights two very different kinds of memory.
quests.explanation: This sentence contrasts factual memory (what was said) with emotional memory (how it felt), a genuinely insightful idea about how people process conflict. The parallel structure makes the contrast easy to follow.
quests.textToSpeak: People rarely remember exactly what was said in an argument, but they remember precisely how it felt.
quests.correctAnswer: People rarely remember exactly what was said in an argument, but they remember precisely how it felt.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] The contrast between 'rarely' and 'precisely' highlights two very different kinds of memory.

quests.hint: 'However small the gesture' concedes a point before making the main claim.
quests.explanation: 'However' plus an adjective again concedes a possible objection (the gesture being small) before making the real point. 'Showing up consistently' as a subject pairs naturally with the singular verb 'tends'.
quests.textToSpeak: However small the gesture, showing up consistently tends to matter more than any single grand one.
quests.correctAnswer: However small the gesture, showing up consistently tends to matter more than any single grand one.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'However small the gesture' concedes a point before making the main claim.

quests.hint: The semicolon links present discomfort to later understanding — pause briefly there.
quests.explanation: This sentence contrasts the present experience of growth with a later, retrospective understanding of it. 'Once you look back' introduces a future point in time from which the present will make more sense.
quests.textToSpeak: Growth rarely feels comfortable while it's happening; it usually only makes sense once you look back.
quests.correctAnswer: Growth rarely feels comfortable while it's happening; it usually only makes sense once you look back.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] The semicolon links present discomfort to later understanding — pause briefly there.

quests.hint: 'Smaller and less dramatic' pairs two related qualities describing the habits.
quests.explanation: 'Shape a life' is a figurative expression for having a lasting influence over time. This closing sentence offers a thoughtful, quietly optimistic idea about the power of small, consistent habits.
quests.textToSpeak: The habits that shape a life are almost always smaller and less dramatic than we tend to imagine.
quests.correctAnswer: The habits that shape a life are almost always smaller and less dramatic than we tend to imagine.
quests.pronunciationTips: [IPA Tip] 'Smaller and less dramatic' pairs two related qualities describing the habits.
